props.title: Live music for a Telluride wedding.
props.lede: A Telluride wedding is the one guests fly in for. The ceremony is up the gondola with the whole box canyon below it, the cocktail hour is on a Mountain Village terrace at nine and a half thousand feet, and the floor fills a lodge, an opera house or a tent in Town Park inside the hours the town allows for amplified sound. So the music is a guitarist who rides up with the guests, a duo for the terrace before the cold comes down, and a band or the DJ for the dancing, with the last song planned to the town’s clock.

headingText.html: It’s one of our weddings bookings: one part of the day or all of it, on one contract with a personal contact through the day, one travel line for the drive and a night’s lodging at cost.

props.title: The three parts of a Telluride wedding day, and what suits each one.
props.lede: The gondola sets the ceremony plan and the altitude sets the sound check. The music rides with the guests from one to the next.

rows.text: One guitarist, acoustic, jazz or Spanish, with a small battery-powered system that carries the officiant’s microphone too, riding up with the guests to an overlook or a ranch on the mountain. Nothing about the ceremony music changes at nine thousand feet except the tuning, which happens twice.

rows.term: The cocktail hour, on a Mountain Village terrace
rows.text: A jazz duo or an acoustic duo, quiet enough to talk across, while the couple is off with the photographer and the light is still on the peaks. The terrace turns cold the moment the sun leaves the canyon, so the hour is timed to the light and moving indoors is agreed before the day.

rows.term: The floor, inside the town’s sound hours
rows.text: A trio or a quartet in a lodge, on the Opera House stage or in a tent in Town Park, or the DJ from the end of dinner to the last song, with that last song planned to the town’s amplified-sound hours rather than discovered at the door. Tejas Singh starts as a duo and finishes as a quartet on one contract, and the wedding jazz band grows through the day the same way.

props.title: On the mountain, in Mountain Village, and in town.

props.html: The mountain holds the ceremony people fly in for. San Sophia Overlook is reached by gondola and looks straight down the canyon at the town, Gorrono Ranch is the on-mountain site for a ceremony and a reception in one place, and Allred’s sits at the top of the gondola with the peaks on one side and the town’s lights on the other once it’s dark. A guitarist and a battery-powered system ride up to any of them; a band plays the ones with power and a floor.

Mountain Village holds the terrace hour and the lodge reception. The Madeline’s terraces take a duo while the light is on the peaks, Mountain Lodge Telluride takes a duo through dinner and a trio for the floor, and both are a gondola ride from a ceremony above them and from the town below, so the day moves without a car.

Town holds the wedding that wants Telluride itself around it. The Sheridan Opera House has a stage and a floor and a hundred years of shows in it, and a band on that stage is the reception the couple remembers, and Town Park, at the box canyon end of Colorado Avenue, takes a tent, a band and the town’s amplified-sound permit.

props.title: Six hours, a night in town, and 9,545 feet.

props.html: Telluride is a far resort from Denver, about six hours each way over the passes, and a band that has driven six hours stays the night. So the quote carries three lines: the fee for the music, one travel line for the drive, and a night’s lodging at cost, meaning the receipt with no markup on it. A winter date is planned with the passes in mind, and the musicians travel a day early when the forecast says so.

The town allows amplified sound under a permit within set hours on Fridays, Saturdays and holidays, and that is the clock the floor is planned to; a ceremony guitarist and a cocktail hour duo sit inside it on their own. The rule is cited and dated on our mountain corridor page, and we confirm the current version with the venue before the day.

Telluride sits at 8,750 feet and Mountain Village at about 9,545. The air is thin and dry, strings drift between an afternoon ceremony and an evening set and get retuned, and anyone singing or playing a horn paces a set differently, so the sound check is longer here than anywhere else we play.

Stage sizes, circuits and input lists for every size are on the technical page, in a form a venue’s events office can check line by line.

items.q: Do you play weddings in Telluride?
items.a: Yes, the whole day or any one part of it, with the fee for the music, one travel line for the drive and a night's lodging at cost on the quote. Every size arrives with sound, setup and pack-down, a certificate of insurance and a W-9. Signet Artists books Telluride weddings from Denver.

items.q: What are Telluride's rules on amplified music at a wedding?
items.a: The town's code allows amplified sound, indoors and out, from 7am to 11pm on Fridays, Saturdays and defined holidays under a permit, as long as it isn't plainly audible beyond what the permit sets. So the floor's last song lands before eleven on a Saturday. We confirm the current version with the venue before the day.

items.q: Can the ceremony be at San Sophia Overlook?
items.a: Yes. The overlook is reached by gondola, so the guitarist and a small battery-powered system ride up with the guests, and the reception happens back in Mountain Village or in town afterward. A ceremony that high is planned for the light and the cold, and the guitarist is set up and tuned well before the first guest steps off the gondola. A ceremony site with power uses the site's own circuit instead.

items.q: How far ahead should we book wedding musicians in Telluride?
items.a: As early as the venue. A Telluride venue books its summer Saturdays well over a year out, the lodging in a small town goes with it, and the musicians' night in town has to be booked as well, so the date is the first thing we need. Tell us the date and the ceremony site and we'll come back quickly with a price for the day, travel and lodging itemized.
